clusterAudits.entity: Cabinet Approves GOBARdhan / National Circular Bioenergy Scheme (₹23,731 Crore)

topicA.title: Cabinet Approves GOBARdhan National Circular Bioenergy Scheme with Outlay of ₹23,731 Crore

topicB.title: Cabinet Approves National Circular Bioenergy Scheme: GOBARdhan (₹23,731 Crore Outlay)

sharedFacts: Total central financial outlay approved: ₹23,731 crore (FY26–FY31).
Umbrella scheme: GOBARdhan (Galvanizing Organic Bio-Agro Resources Dhan).
Implementing ministries: Ministry of Jal Shakti (DDWS), MNRE, MoPNG, and MoA&FW.
uniqueFactsA: Explicit financial allocation breakdown across components: ₹11,250 crore for Bio-CBG plants and ₹7,481 crore for solid bio-manure (FOM/PROM) subsidies.
Target capacity: 500 new commercial Bio-CNG / CBG plants under SATAT initiative.
uniqueFactsB: Targeted agricultural footprint: 200,000 community-level bio-gas units across 50,000 gram panchayats.
Fiscal incentive mechanism: Central Financial Assistance (CFA) up to ₹4 crore per CBG project or 30% of eligible capital cost.
Mandatory CBG blending target: 5% blending of CBG in CNG/PNG by 2028-29.
informationLostIfNaiveDeleteA: Component-level expenditure breakdown (₹11,250 cr CBG + ₹7,481 cr bio-manure) and SATAT integration context.
informationLostIfNaiveDeleteB: CFA grant formula (₹4 cr / 30%), 5% mandatory blending deadline (2028-29), and 200,000 village-level units metric.

topicA.title: Parliament Passes MSMED (Amendment) Bill 2026: Statutory Udyam Status, 90-Day ODR & Mandatory TReDS

topicB.title: MSMED (Amendment) Bill 2026 Passed by Parliament: Judicial, TReDS & Recovery Reforms

sharedFacts: Bill Title: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026.
Statutory amendment to MSMED Act, 2006 passed by Parliament.
Mandatory TReDS onboarding: Expanded to all CPSEs and corporate buyers with turnover exceeding ₹250 crore.
Statutory 45-day payment settlement mandate under Section 15 preserved with strict compound interest penalties.
uniqueFactsA: Statutory permanent Udyam Registration legal status for MSME eligibility in civil litigation.
90-day fast-track Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) mechanism for MSE Facilitation Councils (MSEFCs).
uniqueFactsB: Judicial enforceability: MSEFC awards declared executable as civil court decrees under CPC without separate execution petitions.
Buyer disclosure mandate: Mandatory quarterly filing of delayed MSME payments with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA).
informationLostIfNaiveDeleteA: Udyam registration statutory evidentiary status and 90-day strict ODR timeline.
informationLostIfNaiveDeleteB: Civil court decree status for MSEFC awards and mandatory MCA quarterly delayed payment reporting.

clusterAudits.entity: SEBI Proposes Colour-Coded Credit Risk-o-Meter for Debt Securities

topicA.title: SEBI Proposal: Colour-Coded "Credit Risk-o-Meter" for Debt Securities (~3 min)

topicB.title: SEBI Proposes Colour-Coded "Credit Risk-o-Meter" for Debt Securities

sharedFacts: SEBI standardized 6 colour-coded risk tiers: Irish Green (Lowest risk), Chartreuse (Very low risk), Neon Yellow (Low risk), Caramel (Moderate risk), Dark Orange (Moderate risk of default), Red (High/Very high risk).
Mandatory display by bond issuers and Online Bond Platform Providers (OBPPs).
Multiple CRA rule: Meter must display the lowest rating among all assigned ratings; unsecured debt highlighted in bold red.
uniqueFactsA: Specific OBPP visual format requirement for private placement memorandums.
uniqueFactsB: Visual scale mapping credit ratings from AAA to D across corporate bonds and debt securities.
informationLostIfNaiveDeleteB: AAA to D comprehensive rating mapping matrix.

clusterAudits.entity: CBDT Operationalises FAST-DS (Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers Disclosure Scheme 2026)

topicA.title: FAST-DS Scheme (Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers Disclosure Scheme 2026) (~3 min)

topicB.title: CBDT Operationalises Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers-Disclosure Scheme (FAST-DS), 2026

sharedFacts: CBDT Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers Disclosure Scheme (FAST-DS), 2026.
One-time voluntary disclosure window: August 16 to December 31, 2026.
Statutory authority: Chapter IV (Sections 130–144) of Finance Act, 2026.
Category A (undisclosed foreign assets up to ₹1 crore): 60% total payment (30% tax + 30% penalty/additional charge).
Category B (assets up to ₹5 crore acquired while non-resident or previously taxed): ₹1 lakh flat fee.
uniqueFactsA: Direct comparison between Category A and Category B tax liabilities.
uniqueFactsB: Electronic filing in Form 1, determination order in Form 2, and March 31, 2026 benchmark valuation date.
informationLostIfNaiveDeleteA: Category A vs B tax formula synthesis.
informationLostIfNaiveDeleteB: Form 1 / Form 2 procedural statutory forms and March 31, 2026 valuation benchmark.
